items.title: Clark Terry interviewed by Joe Williams and Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, May 19, 1995
items.q: he’s a very special kid to me because my wife Gwen knows his mother very well

ctx.x: Well you know he’s a very special kid to me because my wife Gwen knows his mother very well. And she headed up a program called STAR, Students Targeting Adult Responsibility. And they were basically responsible for his education. They’ve gotten funds from different sources, now even I kicked in a few bucks, and sent him to Berklee, you know? And he’s still at Berklee, so he came up the hard way, and he came up the soulful way. © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-

Didn’t he? Because it shows. Johnny Pate, whom you know of course, from Chicago, Johnny lives in Las Vegas and he has a radio show on the UNLV station. And he plays Johnny Griffin’s thing with Roy Hargrove, often. And I’m so thrilled that he’s getting some airplay and some attention, because for a while there, I thought that Wynton was the only trumpet player.
Well there’s several of them out there.
